note: Plain-language summary of widely published extension guidance (e.g. FAO, CIMMYT). Reference material for the model, not a diagnosis tool. Single source of truth: the web app imports this file; the Android MaizeGuide is tested against it.

entries.name: Nitrogen deficiency
entries.signs: Yellowing starts at the tip of older, lower leaves and runs down the midrib in a V shape; plants pale and stunted.
entries.distinguish: Lower leaves first (sulfur and zinc show on young leaves first). Common after heavy rain on sandy soil or with no top-dressing.
entries.checkInField: Compare lower and upper leaves; ask when fertilizer was last applied; compare with a well-fertilized row.

entries.name: Waterlogging
entries.signs: Yellowing or purpling and stunting in low parts of the field after heavy rain; roots brown, few, or smelling sour.
entries.distinguish: Follows the lie of the land (low spots) rather than rows or random plants; appears within days of heavy rain.
entries.checkInField: Look for standing water or wet soil after rain; dig up one plant and check roots for brown rot or sour smell.

entries.name: Drought / moisture stress
entries.signs: Leaves roll or curl and look dull grey-green, especially in the afternoon; plants recover overnight if stress is mild.
entries.distinguish: Rolling that eases in the morning points to moisture stress; worst on sandy or shallow soils and ridges.
entries.checkInField: Dig 10 cm down: if soil crumbles dry, moisture is short. Check whether leaves unroll early morning.

entries.name: Sulfur deficiency
entries.signs: Whole young (upper) leaves turn pale yellow, sometimes with light stripes between veins; plants stunted.
entries.distinguish: Upper/younger leaves first — the opposite of nitrogen, which starts on lower leaves.
entries.checkInField: Compare young top leaves with older lower ones. Common on sandy, low-organic-matter soils.

entries.name: Potassium deficiency
entries.signs: Older leaves yellow then brown along the edges (margins) while the midrib stays green; weak stalks may fall over.
entries.distinguish: Edges burn, not the midrib (nitrogen runs down the midrib).
entries.checkInField: Look at lower leaf edges for yellow-brown scorching with a green centre.

entries.name: Phosphorus deficiency
entries.signs: Young plants dark green with purple or reddish leaf edges and tips; slow early growth.
entries.distinguish: Mostly in young plants and cold or wet early-season soils; some varieties are naturally purple.
entries.checkInField: Check whether purple colour is on young plants across an area; compare with plants of the same seed elsewhere.

entries.name: Zinc deficiency
entries.signs: Broad white or pale yellow bands either side of the midrib on young leaves; short internodes.
entries.distinguish: Wide bands near the base of young leaves, not narrow broken streaks (streak virus).
entries.checkInField: Examine young leaves for broad pale bands starting near the leaf base.

entries.name: Fall armyworm
entries.signs: Ragged holes and see-through 'windowpane' patches on leaves; wet sawdust-like droppings (frass) in the whorl; caterpillars inside.
entries.distinguish: Fresh frass in the whorl and a caterpillar with an upside-down Y on its head; damage on scattered plants, not in low spots.
entries.checkInField: Walk a W pattern, check 20 plants: open the whorl, look for frass and caterpillars. Note how many of 20 are damaged.

entries.name: Stalk borer
entries.signs: Rows of small 'shot holes' across leaves as they unroll; dead centre leaf (dead heart); tunnels inside stems.
entries.distinguish: Holes in a neat row across the leaf (from feeding in the whorl) and tunnels in the stalk.
entries.checkInField: Pull the centre leaf: if it slides out and is rotten at the base, split the stem to look for tunnels or larvae.

entries.name: Maize streak virus
entries.signs: Narrow, broken yellow streaks along the veins of young leaves, becoming continuous stripes; plants stunted if infected early.
entries.distinguish: Thin broken streaks along veins (not broad bands); scattered plants, often near field edges; spread by leafhoppers.
entries.checkInField: Hold a young leaf to the light and look for thin broken yellow streaks along veins. Count affected plants.

entries.name: Maize lethal necrosis
entries.signs: Yellow mottling, then drying from leaf edges inward; dead heart; plants may die or cobs rot. Recorded mainly in East Africa.
entries.distinguish: Rapid drying of whole plants and dead heart with mottling; usually needs expert or lab confirmation.
entries.checkInField: Note how many plants are drying from the edges and whether centre leaves are dead. Report to an extension officer.

entries.name: Grey leaf spot
entries.signs: Long, narrow rectangular grey to tan lesions that stop at the leaf veins, starting on lower leaves in humid weather.
entries.distinguish: Straight-sided rectangles bounded by veins (blight lesions are cigar-shaped).
entries.checkInField: Look at lower leaves for rectangular lesions with straight sides.

entries.name: Northern leaf blight
entries.signs: Long cigar- or boat-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on leaves, starting low and moving up in cool, humid weather.
entries.distinguish: Elliptical, cigar-shaped lesions not limited by veins.
entries.checkInField: Measure a few lesions: long (several cm) elliptical lesions suggest blight.

entries.name: Striga (witchweed)
entries.signs: Maize stunted, yellowing and wilting even with moisture, with small weeds with pink or purple flowers at the base.
entries.distinguish: Small pink/purple-flowered weeds attached to maize roots; damage starts before the weed emerges.
entries.checkInField: Look at the base of affected plants for small weeds with pink or purple flowers; carefully dig to see if they attach to roots.
